title: Introduce KMS policy scoring and adaptive audit-sampling guardrails
author: Lena Ortiz
release_notes: Adds a KMS policy scoring engine that produces per-key risk/cost/residency scores and an adaptive audit-sampling decider that dynamically reduces verbose audit traffic for low-risk keys. Includes RBAC v2 policy mappings to block high-risk uses, new metrics and dashboards, and an opt-out flag for enterprise tenants.
description: Motivation: We need a pragmatic guardrail layer between our authorization policies and KMS usage that expresses multi-dimensional risk (residency, provider, customer-specified sensitivity, and cost) and that can reduce high-volume audit noise for clearly low-risk key usages while preserving full audit fidelity for high-risk operations. This PR introduces a lightweight policy scoring service (kms-policy-scoring) and an adaptive audit-sampling decider (audit-sample-decider) that works with RBAC v2 to enforce per-tenant key constraints, surface policy decisions in traces, and provide operators with tunable guardrails. Summary of changes: 1) New library service redwood/kms/policy_scoring: implements a scoring model combining residency match, key origin, provider priority (customer-preferred providers get score bonus), and a per-tenant sensitivity override. Scores are normalized to a 0-100 scale and tagged as LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH. 2) New middleware redwood/edge/audit_sample_decider: consults the scoring service and a tenant-configurable policy to decide sampling rate (0-100%) for detailed audit events (payload-level audit). Sampling decisions are recorded as part of the audit envelope header (X-RW-Audit-Sample) for downstream processing. 3) RBAC v2 mapping updates: policy matcher now rejects KMS operations where score==HIGH unless tenant has explicit 'kms:override' permission. 4) Migration CLI and database migrations: adds tenant config table entries and a one-off migration to backfill default scoring thresholds. 5) Observability: metrics (rw.kms.policy_score, rw.audit.sampling_rate, rw.audit.sampled_events) and a Grafana dashboard JSON. 6) Tests: unit tests for scoring model, integration tests in the eval harness to validate end-to-end behavior across hosted and private deployments, and a small performance microbenchmark for the middleware. Deployment plan and rollouts: Feature is gated behind a runtime flag --enable-kms-policy-scoring and a tenant feature flag. Default rollout: 1) Internal test tenants for 48h, 2) Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with audit sampling set to PASSIVE for LOW score keys, 3) 25% traffic for 72h, 4) global rollout and documentation. Backwards compatibility: Default scoring returns MEDIUM for existing keys so no immediate enforcement; audit-sample-decider defaults to 100% sampling until tenant opt-in or operator rollout changes sampling. Security considerations: scoring decisions are deterministic and signed into the audit envelope to prevent tampering; RBAC checks are applied synchronously before KMS calls to avoid risky fallthroughs. Admins can opt to use an allowlist of providers to force HIGH scores. Monitoring and SLOs: added alerts for sudden drops in sampled events and a dashboard panel showing sample rate by tenant and key. Owner and contacts: Lena Ortiz (author), Priya Shah (security review), Ethan Cole (runtime perf). Related tickets: ENG-8421 (policy scoring), ENG-8479 (audit-sampling), SUP-3124 (support request that motivated sampling controls). review_comments: Priya Shah: Please clarify whether scoring is computed on every request or cached. If cached, what is TTL and how do we prevent stale residency changes?

security_impact: Introduces a new decisioning path in the KMS call flow. Design includes signed audit envelopes and synchronous RBAC enforcement; no key material is persisted. Admin controls allow disabling the scoring engine per tenant.
notes: This PR deliberately keeps the scoring model deterministic and explainable to satisfy compliance teams. The scoring engine is intentionally simple (rule-weighted) rather than ML-driven to make audits and appeals tractable. Future work: add a tenant UI to surface scores and allow safe overrides.
